_purpose: Per-view prompts for the beast's twin cameras, versioned, consumed by restylize_views.py --prompts and by the styled-target-pair submitter. It exists so this subject's generated views are reproducible - the character's canon pair's prompts were never written down and that artifact cannot be rebuilt (E08 director ruling).
_the_pair_reads_stems_1_and_5_only: Handoff 3's pair is view 1 (head-side three-quarter: head, chest, wing leading edges) and view 5 (tail-side three-quarter: tail spines, wing backs, hindquarters) - the identity-dense ends of this subject, confirmed by eye on the Gate 0 renders at pre-flight. All EIGHT stems are written anyway, because beast.json pins views 0-7 on all three framing consumers and a file carrying two stems would make a future eight-view twin run fall back to restylize_views' --prompt default SILENTLY on six views (the tool prints a line, but silence-resolves-to-inheritance is the Finding-B class this repo pays for). Six of these eight have never been generated.
_rule_inherited_from_E02_and_E08: Describe what THAT camera can see and omit what it cannot. Palette and material words are IDENTITY and stay byte-identical across views; only anatomy and framing words change.
_FINDING_the_per_view_rule_bites_here_an: REPORTED, NOT ACTED ON - the dispatch requires byte-equality with the profile's entry and an executor does not hand-trim a fixture. E04-twin-prompts.json justified one constant string across eight views with a reason that is TRUE OF THE SHIP AND FALSE HERE: 'this subject has no view-specific ANATOMY words at all - all twelve fixture elements are material terms'. On the beast, six of the eleven elements name HEAD anatomy - D4 horns, D5 crown and cheek spikes, D8 eyes, D9 tongue, D10 fangs and tooth rows, D11 mouth interior - and view 5 shows no head at all (checked by eye on the Gate 0 render at pre-flight; the head is fully occluded by the body and the near wing). So view 5's prompt asks for six elements its camera cannot see. Two measurements argue this is survivable and neither was taken on a subject with head anatomy: E08's B4 (an exact-silhouette control at IoU 1.000000 locks orientation without the prompt being filtered) and the galleon's pair (all twelve elements in both a bow and a stern three-quarter, 11/12 landing in each). THE PAIR IS THE EVIDENCE: if view 5 comes back with a head grafted onto the hindquarters, or with fangs on the tail, this finding is the cause and the fix is per-view trimming at lane scope - the E10 Ruling 7 move, one level up. If it does not, the ungated string is measured-safe on an anatomy-bearing subject for the first time.
_the_subject_preamble_is_a_FOURTEENTH_te: The string opens 'a winged dragon with deep moss-green scaled hide'. The galleon's opened 'a gilded lion figurehead' - no subject noun at all. So D1's noun phrase is here a with-clause hanging off a subject noun, which is DIFFERENT GRAMMAR from the standalone noun phrase the fixture's form section specifies ('every element is its own noun phrase'; E08 Amendment 13: head noun + minimal modifier lands, stacked compound modifiers drop). Whether D1 lands as well from a with-clause as from a standalone phrase is a question the pair answers and nothing else in the record does. Transcribed as-is; flagged for the ruling.
_backdrop: 'plain lavender-grey background' - RULED, E12 Ruling 8a, not chosen here and not chosen while looking at any result. Low-saturation blue-violet: the one hue family no declared material occupies. It supersedes canon/dragon-materials-estimated.json only as a NAME; the estimated triple (121,121,172) is what the derivation scored and the pair is the first observation of what the word actually realises. The galleon measured that gap at asked 255 -> realised 173 on exactly this recipe, so an ask-vs-realise difference here is expected, not anomalous.
_style_tail: 'visible brushstrokes, painterly worked surface' - the STYLE-SUPPLIED row of canon/DRAGON-IDENTITY.md, byte-identical to the galleon pair's, recorded so a model or LoRA change is noticed rather than absorbed.
_stems_are_pinned_by_the_profile_not_by_: beast.json pins verify/turn_render.py --tag = 'dragonclay' and silhouette_masks.py --tag = 'dragonclay', so the render filenames - and therefore restylize_views' PROMPTS keys - are 'dragonclay_N' by construction. This file cannot drift from them without the profile changing first.
_no_profile_fixture_pointer_exists_yet_F: ship.json carries _fixtures.twin_prompts naming its file; beast.json carries only _fixtures.identity. So nothing in the profile names THIS file, and brush_cloud_step-style provenance checking (which asserts --prompts IS the profile's declared fixture) has no entry to check against on this subject. Reported for the advisor - profile writes are not the executor's.
